content.value_statement: Modern frontend work requires fast interfaces, accessible components, and reliable state patterns. This skill guides React and Next.js implementation with performance, testing, and UX checks.
actual_capabilities: Designs React 19 component structures with hooks, Suspense, and error boundary patterns.
Builds Next.js App Router pages using Server Components, Server Actions, and routing patterns.
Plans responsive layouts with Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules, design tokens, CSS Grid, and Flexbox.
Improves Core Web Vitals through code splitting, image optimization, caching, and bundle analysis.
Adds frontend quality checks with React Testing Library, Playwright, Storybook, Lighthouse CI, and axe-core.
Addresses accessibility with semantic HTML, ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, and color contrast.
limitations: Does not replace live browser testing across every target device.
Does not provide backend-only architecture unless it affects frontend integration.
Requires project context to match existing design systems, data APIs, and build tooling.
Cannot guarantee compatibility with future React, Next.js, or browser releases.

use_cases.title: Launch a Next.js Feature
use_cases.description: Plan and implement App Router pages with server components, client interactions, loading states, and route structure.

use_cases.title: Improve UI Performance
use_cases.description: Identify rendering, bundle, image, caching, and Core Web Vitals issues, then prioritize practical fixes.

use_cases.title: Harden Component Accessibility
use_cases.description: Review components for semantic HTML, keyboard flow, ARIA usage, focus management, and contrast requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Responsive Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a responsive React component for [feature]. Include props, states, accessibility notes, and styling approach for mobile and desktop.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for readability, state handling, and accessibility. Suggest focused changes before editing: [paste component].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Next.js Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Next.js App Router page for Core Web Vitals, data fetching, streaming, and caching. Provide prioritized fixes: [page context].

prompt_templates.title: Design Frontend Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the frontend architecture for [product area] using React 19 and Next.js 15. Include routing, state, testing, and performance strategy.

output_examples.input: Create an accessible data table with sorting and filtering.
output: Component plan with table semantics, keyboard support, and state model.
Responsive behavior for dense and narrow screens.
Testing checklist using axe-core and interaction tests.

output_examples.input: Optimize a slow Next.js dashboard page.
output: Performance diagnosis covering bundle size, data fetching, images, and rendering.
Prioritized fixes for streaming, caching, dynamic imports, and loading states.
Validation steps for Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals.

output_examples.input: Build a design system button for a TypeScript React app.
output: Variant and size model aligned to design tokens.
Accessible interaction states for focus, disabled, loading, and pressed behavior.
Storybook and unit test coverage plan.

best_practices: Provide product goals, target browsers, and device priorities before asking for implementation.
Share existing component conventions and design tokens so outputs match the project.
Ask for validation steps covering accessibility, performance, and tests.
anti_patterns: Requesting large rewrites without explaining current architecture or constraints.
Skipping responsive and accessibility requirements until after implementation.
Using the skill for backend-only work unrelated to frontend behavior.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on React 19, Next.js 15, TypeScript, and common frontend tooling.

faq.question: Can it build complete React components?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide requirements, expected states, data shape, and design constraints for best results.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes semantic HTML, ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, focus management, and contrast checks.

faq.question: Does it replace manual browser testing?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest tests and checks, but real device and browser validation is still required.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Share tokens, component conventions, and examples so the output follows existing patterns.

faq.question: Is it only for Next.js projects?
faq.answer: No. It also supports React application work, but it has strong coverage for Next.js App Router patterns.
